implementation_notes: The language and Foundation own the whole seam: a struct whose stored properties are Codable gets Encodable/Decodable conformance synthesised by the compiler, JSONEncoder().encode(doc) produces the wire Data and JSONDecoder().decode(OrderShipped.self, from: body) rebuilds it, with CodingKeys or keyEncodingStrategy/dateEncodingStrategy fixing wire names and date formats, and optional properties plus decodeIfPresent keeping consumers tolerant of newer producers. Custom wire shapes are handled by implementing init(from:) and encode(to:) with KeyedDecodingContainer rather than by a separate marshaller, so no message class is needed. PropertyListEncoder or a schema-first protobuf library remain options when the peer dictates the format, and hand-written parsing is confined to custom binary protocols.
pitfalls: Synthesised decoding throws keyNotFound for a missing non-optional property, so additive evolution requires Option/decodeIfPresent on every field a producer may omit.
Date handling defaults differ: JSONEncoder's default strategy writes a Double reference-date timestamp and Data as base64, which is rarely what a cross-language consumer expects.
Enums that are RawRepresentable throw on unknown raw values, so a document carrying a new enum case breaks older clients unless a fallback case or custom init(from:) exists.
Struct documents are value types, but a decoded document holding large Data still copies on pass-through; big payloads want streaming or a claim check.
